comment: Declarative registry of every third-party asset. Nothing binary is committed:
`npm run assets:fetch` downloads into public/assets/, verifies the hash, and
regenerates CREDITS.md. `npm run assets:verify` runs in CI and fails on an
unlicensed entry, a missing attribution, or a hash mismatch.
sha256 null means the hash has not been recorded yet. Run
`npm run assets:fetch -- --record` on a machine that can reach the host and
the hash is written back here, pinning the file from then on.
EVERY asset here is optional. role 'flora' means a model that replaces one
species' procedural shape in src/config/flora.js; with none of them fetched
the valley is drawn entirely out of procedural geometry and is complete. See
rule 4 in CLAUDE.md — this is the rule the whole renderer is built around.
The art direction is Quaternius's Stylized Nature MegaKit, and the pack.nature
entries are the pack itself. quaternius.com and itch.io are both blocked by
this environment's egress policy, so they are pinned to a commit of a CC0
mirror (see each entry's `mirror`) on raw.githubusercontent.com, which is
reachable. The models there are repacked: meshopt-compressed and quantised,
so the glTF loader MUST register a Meshopt decoder — see src/assets/loader.js.
Kenney's kit fills the two gaps the free MegaKit tier has — palm and cactus.
What is NOT pinned here is as deliberate as what is. The pack's grass, clover,
pebbles and flowers are lovely and cost 150-1700 triangles each; this scene
plants forty thousand of those, and swapping them in took one frame from three
million triangles to twenty-four. Anything planted by the tens of thousands
keeps its procedural shape, which is a tenth of the cost. See docs/ROADMAP.md
— level of detail is what would let them in.
Every URL is pinned to a commit rather than a branch. A branch URL would
drift and fail its own recorded hash the next time upstream pushed.
A 'local' provenance also exists for files this environment cannot fetch at
all: it names the pack and waits for a human, and `npm run assets:link --
<folder>` matches a downloaded pack onto those slots. Nothing uses it today.
